**Gini coefficient for the United States (most recent estimates)**  

| Source | Year | Gini coefficient |
|--------|------|------------------|
| OECD | 2019 | **0.41** |
| World Bank | 2018 | 0.421 |

> **Interpretation**  
> A Gini coefficient of 0.41–0.42 indicates a moderate level of income inequality in the U.S., higher than many European countries but lower than some developing economies.

> **Why the numbers differ**  
> - The OECD uses household income data and applies its own methodology.  
> - The World Bank uses national accounts data and a slightly different calculation.  
> - Both figures are based on the most recent data available; newer surveys (e.g., the U.S. Census Bureau’s Current Population Survey) may update the estimate in the coming months.

If you need the exact figure for a specific year or a more detailed breakdown (by state, age group, etc.), let me know!
